msg: This file describes encryption but carries no export-control notice. EAR 742.15(b) attaches to the act of publishing the source, not to the release notes.
No crypt@bis.doc.gov in the notice. EAR 742.15(b)(1) asks for an email to BIS with the internet location of the published source code.
No enc@nsa.gov in the notice. The same 742.15(b)(1) notification goes to the ENC Encryption Request Coordinator as well as to BIS.
The notice names no internet location. The URL you emailed is the notification; a notice without it cannot be checked against what BIS received.
No ECCN in the notice (5D002, 5E002, 5A002 or 5D992). Publicly available encryption source code is classified before it is published, not after.
This notice cites License Exception TSU / EAR 740.13(e) for encryption source code. BIS removed that paragraph in the 20 September 2016 encryption rule and moved the notification to 742.15(b).

The notice claims the code is outside export control (or EAR99) because it is open source. Public availability under 742.15(b) is conditioned on the notification; it is not automatic and EAR99 is not a classification for 5D002 encryption source.
The notice records no date for the notification. Without a date nobody can tell which release the email covered.
The recorded notification is from an earlier calendar year. Re-notify on a new internet location, and check the annual self-classification report due 1 February.
The notice does not say what happens when the source moves. EAR 742.15(b)(1) wants a fresh email whenever the internet location changes.
